title: Gen Z flocks to BirdTok as birding takes flight: ‘It’s a craving for something real’

paragraphs.en: Sorry Elon, but they’re not your kind of tweets. Social media users are flocking to TikTok to join a burgeoning trend for birding videos as the hobby attracts a younger demographic.
paragraphs.zh: 抱歉了，埃隆，但它们可不是你那种“推文”（tweets）。社交媒体用户正纷纷涌向TikTok，加入日益兴起的观鸟视频潮流，这一爱好正吸引着更年轻的群体。

paragraphs.en: With the internet ever more cluttered with polarising, shouty and AI content, evidence is emerging of Britons preferring a gentler, more melodic window on the world in the shape of footage of the nation’s feathered friends.
paragraphs.zh: 随着互联网上的内容越来越充斥着两极分化、喧嚣嘈杂的争吵和AI内容，有证据表明，英国人更喜欢用更柔和、更具韵律感的窗口看世界，那就是观看本国带羽毛的朋友们的视频。

paragraphs.en: TikTok says UK posts of #birdwatching and #birdtok videos have risen by a third over the past three months as users flock to feathered friend content. The number of #birding posts has risen by 40% in the UK and the global number of posts carrying one of those three hashtags now stands at 1m. A video of Steven, a relatively tame seagull , being fed raw Tesco salmon fillet has more than 52m views.
paragraphs.zh: TikTok表示，过去三个月里，英国带#birdwatching（观鸟）和#birdtok标签的帖子数量增长了三分之一，用户纷纷涌向这类鸟类内容。英国带#birding标签的帖子数量增长了40%，全球带这三个标签之一的帖子总数现已达到100万条。一段视频拍摄的是一只相对温顺的海鸥“史蒂文”被喂食乐购生鲑鱼鱼排，观看次数已超过5200万。

paragraphs.en: Posts by the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds have received nearly 9m views over the past year, with a third of those coming from under-24s. Dedicated birders say the boom is down to the popularity of apps such as Merlin – a kind of Shazam for birdsong – a resurgence in curiosity about the natural world, a desire for analogue hobbies and the power of social media.
paragraphs.zh: 皇家鸟类保护协会发布的帖子在过去一年获得了近900万次观看，其中三分之一来自24岁以下的用户。资深观鸟者表示，这股热潮要归功于Merlin等应用的流行——它就像鸟类鸣叫的“Shazam”音乐识别工具——人们对自然世界的好奇心重新抬头、对模拟（analogue）爱好的渴望，以及社交媒体的力量。

paragraphs.en: “It’s a craving for something ‘real’ and birding is a really nice gateway to that,” says Jack Baddams , 33, a Derbyshire-based bird enthusiast whose videos about tagging birds have had millions of views.
paragraphs.zh: “这是对某种‘真实’东西的渴望，而观鸟是通往这种体验的一个绝佳入口。”33岁的杰克·巴达姆斯说。他是德比郡的鸟类爱好者，其关于给鸟类佩戴脚环的视频已获得数百万次观看。

paragraphs.en: “Anyone can walk outside or look out of their window and see a bird. And there are communities that build off the back of that.”
paragraphs.zh: “任何人都可以走到户外，或者望向窗外，看到一只鸟。而且还有以此为纽带建立起来的社群。”

paragraphs.en: Baddams, who has 300,000 followers, is a TV researcher and one of 3,000 bird “ringers” for the British Trust for Ornithology, who places identification rings around birds to help monitor phenomena such as population changes or migratory patterns. A video on his account explaining the craft of bird ringing has had 7.5m views
paragraphs.zh: 拥有30万粉丝的巴达姆斯是一名电视研究员，也是英国鸟类学信托基金会的3000名鸟类“环志员”之一。环志员会给鸟戴上识别环，以帮助监测种群变化或迁徙模式等现象。他账号上一条讲解鸟类环志技艺的视频已获得750万次观看。

paragraphs.en: Baddams admits he has been “shocked” by the scale of interest.
paragraphs.zh: 巴达姆斯承认，人们对这一兴趣的规模之大让他感到“震惊”。
